analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page defines drag dependencies, presents drag equation with coefficient density velocity and reference area, explains choices for reference area, notes experimental determination and dynamic pressure

overview.headline: Drag force expressed through coefficient density speed and reference area

keyPoints.point: Drag depends on density and square of velocity along with viscosity and shape effects
keyPoints.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity

keyPoints.point: Drag equation states that drag equals drag coefficient times density times half velocity squared times reference area
keyPoints.quote: The drag equation states that drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd times the density rho (ρ) times half of the velocity V squared

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel for measurement
keyPoints.quote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.

keyPoints.point: Reference area in drag equation is chosen as a measurable area and must be specified when reporting coefficients
keyPoints.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyPoints.point: Combination of density times square of velocity divided by two is called dynamic pressure in pressure relation
keyPoints.quote: The combination of terms “density times the square of the velocity divided by two” is called the dynamic pressure

keyTerms.gloss: variable that collects complex dependence into single drag value
keyTerms.quote: For drag, this variable is called the drag coefficient, designated “Cd.”

keyTerms.gloss: combination term of density and velocity that contributes to pressure description
keyTerms.quote: The combination of terms “density times the square of the velocity divided by two” is called the dynamic pressure

keyTerms.gloss: chosen area that characterizes size dependence for aerodynamic force
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: facility where drag is measured experimentally using controlled airflow
keyTerms.quote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.

keyTerms.gloss: property of air designated by rho that appears in dynamic pressure term
keyTerms.quote: In the equation given above, the density is designated by the letter rho (ρ).

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Reinforces factual retention of definitions before learners compare how reference choices alter coefficient values
componentPlan.focusQuote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Shows how same drag value yields different coefficients depending on which measurable area is chosen for reporting
componentPlan.focusQuote: If we think of drag as being caused by friction between the air and the body, a logical choice would be the total surface area of the body.
